Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

legal adjective

allowed by law

also lawful, legally, legitimate, is it legal?, legal age, illegal, lawfully

classical

Liv. 25.2.6: quod nōndum ad petendum lēgitima aetās esset
Traupman 196, 339: legal

lēgitimus, lēgitima, lēgitimum

adjective

lawful, legal: fixed or allowed by law

The legal age is aetās lēgitima; legally is lēgitimē or lēge (Traupman 196). Traupman also gives secundum lēgem (or lēgēs). What is illegal is contrā lēgēs.

Other words

  • per lēgēs licet — it is legal: the laws allow it

    phrase: licet, impersonal, “it is allowed” · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 43: nihil, quod per lēgēs licēret (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s way of saying that something is legal.

  • licitus, licita, licitum — permitted, lawful

    adjective · also used · classical · Tac. Ann. 15.37: per licita atque illicita (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētica: Verg.; also post-Augustan prose (Tac.))

    Lewis & Short: poetic and post-Augustan, for classical permissus.

  • lēgitimē — legally, lawfully

    also used · classical · Traupman 179

Examples

  • huic petentī aedīlitātem cum obsisterent tribūnī plēbis, negantēs ratiōnem ejus habendam esse quod nōndum ad petendum lēgitima aetās esset, sī mē, inquit, omnēs Quirītēs aedīlem facere volunt, satis annōrum habeō

    When the tribunes of the people opposed his standing for the aedileship, saying he could not be considered because he was not yet of the legal age to stand, he said: “If all the citizens want to make me aedile, I am old enough.”Liv. 25.2.6–7

  • lēgitimē, lēge

    legallyTraupman 196

See also law, legal, rule.
